comments.body:
Plan-review remediation for 73b8-2d79-3046-44ce (2026-08-21). Every claim below was checked
against the worktree /Users/joeoakhart/impl-2ddd-consolidation. No file was modified.

WHAT WAS FACTUALLY WRONG IN THE ORIGINAL PLAN

1. The backlog was never sized, and it is enormous. The plan said to add PLW1510 and the whole PT
   family to ruff `select`, "clearing the existing backlog in the same change". Actual counts on
   this tree with ruff 0.16.3 over `src tests scripts` (the exact scope `make lint` uses):
     PLW1510  336   subprocess-run-without-check   -- ZERO auto-fixes, even with --unsafe-fixes
     PT (all) 1811                                 -- only 37 safely auto-fixable
   PT breakdown: PT018 1513, PT011 84, PT019 69, PT006 57, PT001 37, PT022 19, PT017 15, PT007 7,
   PT013 4, PT008 2, PT021 2, PT012 1, PT028 1.
   That is 2147 findings, of which 2110 are hand edits. A single story cannot absorb that, and a
   plan that adopts the rules without saying so is not implementable as written.

2. The proposed escape hatch fails an existing guard test. The plan said stylistic PT findings
   "go in `ignore` with a comment, not per-line noqa". tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py:73
   (test_ruff_ignore_is_exactly_the_ruf_unicode_deferral) asserts
   `[tool.ruff.lint].ignore == ["RUF001", "RUF002", "RUF003"]` EXACTLY, and
   test_ruff_lint_has_no_extend_ignore forbids `extend-ignore`. Adding anything to `ignore` turns
   that test red. The project already documents the right pattern in the same config block: "We
   take SIM115 only, not the wider SIM group" — select individual codes.

3. Dropping --timeout=300 from CI fails a second existing guard.
   tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:718
   (test_every_ci_pytest_lane_has_a_per_test_hang_guard) sweeps EVERY workflow pytest step and
   asserts both "--timeout=" and "--timeout-method=thread" are present, with a docstring naming
   tickets 89d5-61da-b621-47f8 and d835-1846-95d1-4d84 as why. The plan's step 2 ("drop
   --timeout=300 from the CI invocation so the ini value applies") would have turned it red.

4. The CI citation was off by one step, and eleven other lanes went unmentioned. The plan cited
   ".github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:656-672". `grep -n -- "--timeout=" .github/workflows/`
   shows _build-and-test.yml carries the flag on TWO steps, :658 (default tier) and :673
   (integration tier) — the cited range covers the first and misses the second. Eleven further
   pytest lanes carry their own budgets: external-integration.yml:245 (900), :405 (600), :514
   (300), :625 (900), :765 (1800); _optionality.yml:140 (600), :165 (300); _eval-discipline.yml:74
   (300); test.yml:144 (600); structured-output-baseline.yml:117 (3600). None were in Scope.

5. PLW1510 was scoped to tests/** only. The plan's Scope listed `tests/**`, but `make lint` runs
   `ruff check $(sources)` with `sources = src tests scripts` (Makefile:13). 318 of the 336
   PLW1510 findings are under src+tests and 336 under src+tests+scripts, so src/ and scripts/ are
   in the sweep whether the plan says so or not.

6. The behavioural probe was unfalsifiable after landing. AC2 proposed a probe "removed before
   landing or kept ... with the slow one marked". A test that must fail cannot be committed, so
   the negative arm would simply not exist in the tree afterwards. The corrected plan keeps a
   permanent tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py whose negative arm runs a generated test in a
   subprocess and asserts the Timeout failure there.

WHAT I CORRECTED

- Replaced "add PT" with per-code selection: PLW1510 plus PT001, PT006, PT007, PT008, PT012,
  PT013, PT017, PT021, PT022, PT028 = 481 findings, verified by running the combined selector.
  PT018/PT011/PT019 (1666 findings) are named as deliberately deferred, in the config comment as
  well as the plan, so the omission reads as a decision.
- Replaced "drop the CI flags" with "lower them to 20", keeping --timeout-method=thread so the
  hang-guard sweep stays green, plus a new drift assertion pinning the two lanes equal to the ini
  `timeout`.
- Added the eleven out-of-scope lanes with the reason they keep their own budgets.
- Widened Scope to src/** and scripts/** for the PLW1510 sweep, and added
  tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py; listed test_ruff_ratchet.py as reviewed-but-unchanged
  (unchanged precisely because `ignore` is no longer touched).
- Sequenced marking before lowering, and made the marking step an INTEGRATION-tier measurement,
  because the unit tier turned out to need no marks at all (below).

CLAIMS THAT SURVIVED VERIFICATION UNCHANGED

- pytest-timeout==2.4.0 really is pinned, at pyproject.toml:251, and is installed in the venv.
- scripts/check_wall_clock_asserts.py and scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py exist, run in CI at
  _build-and-test.yml:181-198 (each behind an `if [ -f ]` tree-skew guard), and are absent from
  `make lint`. Both exit 0 on the current tree, so adding them changes reachability, not verdict.
- `make -n lint | grep -c "check_wall_clock_asserts.py\|check_raw_git_writes.py"` prints 0 today,
  and the same grep for check_comment_hygiene prints 1 — so AC3 is non-vacuous and the cited
  precedent is real.
- Ruff selects exactly ["E","F","W","I","UP","B","BLE001","T201","SIM115","ASYNC","DTZ","RUF"];
  neither PLW1510 nor any PT code is enabled.
- All four cited bug aliases resolve, and all four are closed bugs:
  obvious-saline-gerbil = 0e1d-c698-c38d-4c3e, sound-bumpkinly-thrush = 1241-b83c-f8c7-40bf,
  albinic-kyanite-goldeneye = e394-9433-c839-4c9f, tapestried-abhorrent-tuna = 9bb7-4430-1202-4d93.
- aciduric-enhanced-piranha = 2d9a-78c5-5f87-4a22, a closed task, "comment-hygiene gate is
  reachable locally only via the full suite, not make lint" — exactly the precedent claimed.

MEASUREMENTS

Ruff statistics (env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" ruff check --statistics <sel> src tests scripts):
  --select PLW1510                        -> 336 errors, no fixable line
  --select PLW1510 --unsafe-fixes         -> 336 errors, still no fixes offered
  --select PLW1510 (src tests only)       -> 318 errors
  --select PT                             -> 1811 errors; 37 fixable with --fix,
                                             1358 hidden fixes behind --unsafe-fixes
  --select PLW1510,PT001,PT006,PT007,PT008,PT012,PT013,PT017,PT021,PT022,PT028 src tests scripts
                                          -> 481 errors, exit 1 (this is the corrected plan's
                                             first acceptance criterion, failing today as it must)

Timeout budget, the load-bearing measurement:
  env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest -m unit -n 4 --dist worksteal -q \
      -p no:cacheprovider --timeout=20 --timeout-method=thread
  -> 6 failed, 5097 passed, 8 skipped, 2 warnings, 4 errors in 676.35s (0:11:16)
  -> `grep -c "Failed: Timeout\|+++ Timeout"` over the log: 0
  -> the 10 failures/errors are all the environmental guard "The repo HEAD moved during this
     test" (8 occurrences), caused by a concurrent job committing in this worktree mid-run — not
     the budget.
  Conclusion: NO unit-tier test exceeds 20 seconds. The scary-looking numbers I had catalogued
  from the sources — tests/unit/test_live_jira_xdist_confinement.py:177 (300),
  tests/unit/test_jira_dc_capability_map_workflow.py:143 (300),
  tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:855 (300), tests/unit/test_ci_actionlint_install.py:70
  (180), tests/unit/grounding/test_yield_eval.py:82 (180),
  tests/unit/test_amend_msg_change_id.py:141 (120),
  tests/unit/test_candidate_tracing_oracle.py:287 (120),
  tests/interfaces/store/test_ensure_invariants.py:152 (120) — are subprocess CEILINGS, not
  observed durations. Only 4 @pytest.mark.timeout marks exist tree-wide
  (tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:1806 -> 3; tests/unit/test_opcert_service_app.py:158 -> 2,
  :206 -> 2, :268 -> 60). The integration tier has not been run this way and still needs its own
  measurement before its lane is lowered.

Mechanism proof (throwaway project, this worktree's venv):
  pyproject.toml with addopts = "--strict-markers --strict-config", timeout = 20,
  timeout_method = "thread", timeout_func_only = true
  -> an unmarked test sleeping 25 s fails with "+++++++ Timeout +++++++"
  -> the same test carrying @pytest.mark.timeout(60, func_only=True) passes in 25.01s
  Also confirmed by reading pytest_timeout's source: parser.addini("timeout", ...),
  addini("timeout_method", ...), addini("timeout_func_only", ..., type="bool", default=False) are
  real ini options in 2.4.0, so --strict-config accepts them and a TOML integer works for
  `timeout`.

Config assertions used as acceptance criteria, run on the current tree to confirm they fail:
  python -c "...['tool']['ruff']['lint']['select']; assert 'PLW1510' in s and 'PT001' in s"
    -> AssertionError: ['E','F','W','I','UP','B','BLE001','T201','SIM115','ASYNC','DTZ','RUF']
  python -c "...['tool']['pytest']['ini_options']; assert p['timeout']==20 ..."
    -> KeyError: 'timeout'

AC EVIDENCE, verified against merged main (Gerrit 2100, LLM-Review +1 / Verified +1).

AC1 adopted codes clean tree-wide: ruff check --select PLW1510,PT001,PT006,PT007,PT008,PT012,PT013,PT017,PT021,PT022,PT028 src tests scripts exits 0 (was 481 findings).
AC2 configured, not ad hoc: PLW1510 and PT001 both present in [tool.ruff.lint].select.
AC3 [tool.ruff.lint].ignore unchanged: test_ruff_ratchet.py 15 passed - which now includes the three membership tests review asked for, pinning the adopted PT subset in both directions and rejecting a bare PT group selector.
AC4 budget in the ini: timeout==20, timeout_method=='thread', timeout_func_only is True.
AC5 both budget arms hold under the ini alone: test_timeout_budget.py 3 passed.
AC6 the two CI lanes carry the budget and keep the hang guard: the grep prints 2, and test_ci_workflow_parity.py 25 passed with the drift assertion in place.
AC7 make lint reaches both hygiene checks: make -n lint matches check_wall_clock_asserts.py / check_raw_git_writes.py exactly 2 times (was 0).
AC9 make lint exits 0.

AC8 - satisfied on its stated terms, with an anomaly recorded rather than smoothed over. The criterion is that 'pytest -m unit -n 4 --dist worksteal' reports NO 'Failed: Timeout'. It reports ZERO, so the criterion holds: 5430 passed, 8 skipped, 340.30s. But the run also produced one non-timeout failure - test_conformance.py::test_opengrep_timeout_via_harness, 'worker gw0 crashed while running it'. In isolation that test PASSES in 44.46s, and CI is green on this change across all four shards. I did not reproduce the crash a second time and am not asserting a cause; the observation is recorded on task lead-unpleasing-kitten (7da8-9d47-9604-4257), which already owns that test and names it as retaining a real scan timeout. Ticking AC8 reflects its literal check passing, not a claim that the tier is unconditionally clean.

Review and CI both found real defects in this change, and both were fixed rather than argued with: the gate's own adopt/defer decision had no oracle (now pinned in test_ruff_ratchet.py and mutation-proven three ways), the PT022 conversion left rebar_repo annotated -> Iterator[Path] with a 'Yields' docstring after becoming return-based, 25b4's uniqueness guard fired on the new test_timeout_budget.py launching pytest directly, and wiring the two gates into make lint broke a synthetic-repo test that needed their scripts stubbed.

comments.body:
CLOSE GATE CAUGHT THE file_impact GAP - the sixth in this epic, and the widest. The recorded impact listed only the config and test files; the landed commits touch 318 files, because adopting PLW1510 tree-wide means every subprocess.run in src/, scripts/ and tests/ has to state its check= policy.

file_impact now declares all 318 with per-file reasons: the config/CI/docs files individually (pyproject.toml for the select list and the pytest budget, Makefile for reaching the two hygiene gates, _build-and-test.yml for the two lanes' --timeout flags, local-dev-env.md), the named test files individually (test_ruff_ratchet.py's membership pins, test_timeout_budget.py's two arms, interfaces/conftest.py's PT022 conversion, test_check_criteria_vocabulary.py's new stubs), and the rest by category - PLW1510 explicit check= for src/ and scripts/, flake8-pytest-style fixes for tests/.

Worth stating plainly: a 318-path declaration is not a satisfying artefact, and the gate's design assumes a change touches a scope an author can enumerate meaningfully. A tree-wide lint adoption is the case where that assumption strains. The declaration is accurate and the gate is right to demand it - a silent 318-file diff against a 12-path plan is exactly what it exists to stop - but the honest reading is that this story's shape and the gate's granularity are a poor fit, not that the record was carelessly kept. rebar offers only per-path entries or --none; there is no 'wide sweep, these categories' form, and --none would have been a false statement here.

Running tally of this failure mode across the epic: 1cf6, 7931, a73e, d6e3, 1dd5 and now 73b8 - six of them. Every one was caught by the close gate and none by anything earlier.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Twenty-seven bugs in the fortnight defect review were tests that could not fail or that burned CI time: absent-string subprocess oracles with no return-code check (`0e1d-c698-c38d-4c3e`, `1241-b83c-f8c7-40bf`), a test burning the full 120 s Jira readiness budget per xdist worker (`e394-9433-c839-4c9f`), a timeout oracle expiring after its watchdog fires (`9bb7-4430-1202-4d93`). All closed.

State of the tree:

- `pytest-timeout==2.4.0` is pinned at `pyproject.toml:251`.
- `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` sets `addopts = "--strict-markers --strict-config"` but no `timeout` / `timeout_method` / `timeout_func_only`, so `make test` and bare local `pytest` have no per-test budget. Only 4 `@pytest.mark.timeout` marks exist tree-wide (`test_review_bot.py:1806`; `test_opcert_service_app.py:158,206,268`).
- The budget lives only on CI command lines: `_build-and-test.yml:658` (default tier) and `:673` (integration tier), both `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread`.
- Ruff 0.16.3 selects `E,F,W,I,UP,B,BLE001,T201,SIM115,ASYNC,DTZ,RUF` with `ignore = ["RUF001","RUF002","RUF003"]`; no `PLW1510`, no `PT`. `make lint` runs `ruff check $(sources)`, `sources = src tests scripts` (`Makefile:13`).
- `scripts/check_wall_clock_asserts.py` and `check_raw_git_writes.py` exist, run in CI only (`_build-and-test.yml:181-198`), are absent from `make lint`, and both exit 0 today.

Backlog (`ruff check --statistics src tests scripts`): **PLW1510 = 336, zero fixes even under `--unsafe-fixes`**; **PT = 1811**, only 37 safely auto-fixable — PT018 1513, PT011 84, PT019 69, PT006 57, PT001 37, PT022 19, PT017 15, PT007 7, PT013 4, PT008 2, PT021 2, PT012 1, PT028 1.

Runtime: `pytest -m unit -n 4 --dist worksteal -q --timeout=20 --timeout-method=thread` ran 11 m 16 s, 5097 passed, **zero** `Failed: Timeout` (the 6 failures + 4 errors were the environmental "repo HEAD moved" guard). The `timeout=120..300` values in test sources are subprocess ceilings, not durations: the unit tier already fits inside 20 s. The integration tier is not yet measured.

Operator decision (2026-08-21): adopt only common practice in maintained OSS projects; a 20 s per-test budget with an explicit override for tests that must be slow.

## Approach
1. **Ruff, per code.** Add the eleven codes in the first AC's selector to `[tool.ruff.lint] select` — 481 findings, cleared here. `PT018`/`PT011`/`PT019` (1666) are deliberately NOT selected; the `select` comment says so in place. PLW1510 is cleared with explicit `check=False` where the call already inspects `returncode`, `check=True` only where an unchecked non-zero exit is a bug.
2. **Local budget in the ini.** Add the three keys in the fourth AC to `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`.
3. **Mark the slow integration tests.** Measure that tier at `--timeout=20`, then give each over-budget test `@pytest.mark.timeout(N, func_only=True)` with a one-line comment naming why. No exemption without a comment.
4. **Lower, do not drop, the CI flags.** `_build-and-test.yml:658` and `:673` go `--timeout=300` -> `20`, keeping `--timeout-method=thread`.
5. **Drift guard.** One new assertion in `test_ci_workflow_parity.py`: the `--timeout=` on those two steps equals the ini `timeout`.
6. **`make lint` reachability.** Append both hygiene scripts to the `lint` recipe, as `check_comment_hygiene.py` was by task `2d9a-78c5-5f87-4a22`. No `if [ -f ]` guard: `make lint` runs the patchset's own Makefile.

Not adopted (no maintained tool does it): lints for subprocess `timeout=`, `sleep` budgets, `os.environ.copy()`, `sys.modules` writes, foreign `.git/` writes.

## Constraints
- **PT codes go in `select`, never `ignore`.** `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py:73` (`test_ruff_ignore_is_exactly_the_ruf_unicode_deferral`) asserts `[tool.ruff.lint].ignore == ["RUF001","RUF002","RUF003"]` exactly, and `test_ruff_lint_has_no_extend_ignore` forbids `extend-ignore`, so selecting a family then silencing most of it fails CI. Per-code selection is the project's own precedent: the `[tool.ruff.lint]` comment records "We take SIM115 only, not the wider SIM group".
- **`--timeout=` must not be removed from any workflow.** `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:718` (`test_every_ci_pytest_lane_has_a_per_test_hang_guard`) sweeps every workflow pytest step and requires both `--timeout=` and `--timeout-method=thread` (`89d5-61da-b621-47f8`, `d835-1846-95d1-4d84`). Dropping them so the ini applies turns that guard red.
- **Eleven other `--timeout=` lanes stay untouched**, each calibrated for external / live-service / eval suites that run for minutes: `external-integration.yml:245,405,514,625,765`, `_optionality.yml:140,165`, `_eval-discipline.yml:74`, `test.yml:144`, `structured-output-baseline.yml:117`.
- **PLW1510 is not test-only.** 318 of the 336 sit under `src` + `tests`; `make lint` covers all three trees.
- **The ini mechanism is verified**, so only the marking sweep is open: the three keys are real `parser.addini` options in pytest-timeout 2.4.0, and on this venv they time out an unmarked 25 s test under `--strict-config` and pass the same test marked `timeout(60, func_only=True)`.
- Marking precedes lowering: step 3 before step 4.

## Scope
`pyproject.toml` (ruff `select`; pytest ini keys); `Makefile` (`lint`); `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` (`:658`, `:673`); `tests/**` + `src/**` + `scripts/**` (the PLW1510 and selected-PT backlog); `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` (drift assertion); `tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py` (new); `docs/local-dev-env.md` (budget + override).

Reviewed, NOT changed: `test_ruff_ratchet.py`; the nine other workflow lanes; the two hygiene scripts.

## Testing
`tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py` holds both arms: a ~25 s test marked `timeout(60, func_only=True)` that passes, and a negative arm running `pytest` on a generated temp test in a subprocess with no `--timeout`, asserting a `Timeout` failure (a permanently red test cannot be committed). Pinning: `test_ruff_ratchet.py`, `test_ci_workflow_parity.py` and the two hygiene-lint tests stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria
All commands run from the worktree with `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"` prepended.
- [x] The adopted codes are clean tree-wide. `ruff check --select PLW1510,PT001,PT006,PT007,PT008,PT012,PT013,PT017,PT021,PT022,PT028 src tests scripts` exits 0; today it exits 1 with 481 findings.
- [x] They are configured, not passed ad hoc. `python -c "import tomllib; s=tomllib.load(open('pyproject.toml','rb'))['tool']['ruff']['lint']['select']; assert 'PLW1510' in s and 'PT001' in s"` exits 0. Today: `AssertionError`.
- [x] `[tool.ruff.lint].ignore` is unchanged. `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py -q` exits 0 (pinning).
- [x] The budget lives in the ini. `python -c "import tomllib; p=tomllib.load(open('pyproject.toml','rb'))['tool']['pytest']['ini_options']; assert p['timeout']==20 and p['timeout_method']=='thread' and p['timeout_func_only'] is True"` exits 0. Today: `KeyError: 'timeout'`.
- [x] Both budget arms hold under the ini alone. `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py -q` exits 0. Today pytest exits 4.
- [x] The two CI lanes carry the ini budget and keep their hang guard. `grep -c -- "--timeout=20 --timeout-method=thread" .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` prints `2` (today `0`), and `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py -q` exits 0 with the drift assertion in place.
- [x] `make lint` reaches both hygiene checks. `make -n lint | grep -c "check_wall_clock_asserts.py\|check_raw_git_writes.py"` prints `2`; today `0`.
- [x] The default tier stays clean under the budget. `python -m pytest -m unit -n 4 --dist worksteal -q` reports no `Failed: Timeout` (pinning; measured clean 2026-08-21 at an explicit `--timeout=20`).
- [x] `make lint` exits 0.
